ass:overlap.detail: The paper gives exactly the two inequalities in the Lean definition.

ass:score-marginal.detail: The Lean definition identifies the score pushforward of P with H.

ass:randomized-assignment.detail: The Lean integral identity expresses the stated conditional assignment probability almost surely.

ass:consistency.detail: The Lean predicate sets the observed outcome equal to the potential outcome selected by the assigned arm almost surely.

ass:deterministic-release.detail: The Lean predicate sets the released label equal to g of the score almost surely.

def:sharp-ate-set.detail: The Lean definition gives exactly the stated closed interval for compatible released-law cell masses.

def:worst-case-ambiguity.detail: The Lean supremum ranges over the stated causal-law class and uses the width of the corresponding sharp ATE interval.

ass:density-lower.detail: The density identity and almost-everywhere lower bound match DensityLower; measurability is implicit in calling f a density.

ass:released-law.detail: The paper equates the released law under P with the specified released measure, as Lean does.

def:causal-law-class.detail: The four stated conditions define the same probability-law class; measurability of the release rule is incidental regularity.

def:compatible-law-class.detail: The class adds equality with the released law to the same causal-law conditions.

def:arm-cell-primitives.detail: The cell masses, conditional outcome laws, tilted score laws, and reciprocal weights match the Lean definitions, with mass compatibility stated for the endpoint formulas.

def:mean-endpoints.detail: Both quantile formulas and the positive-cell sum match the Lean definitions under CompatibleCellMasses.

ass:external-log-independent.detail: Lean states that, for every admissible law pair, the joint trial and log law equals the product of its trial and log marginals.

def:external-law-class.detail: The class has the stated probability, overlap, score-marginal, assignment, consistency, and deterministic-release conditions.

def:external-experiment.detail: Lean defines the joint law as the product of independent released trial draws and independent score-log draws.

def:external-honest-procedures.detail: Lean imposes the stated uniform coverage requirement under the external experiment.

def:external-excess-risk.detail: Lean takes the infimum over honest intervals of the supremum expected positive excess length relative to the sharp interval.

def:score-lower-density-class.detail: A probability score law with a measurable density bounded below almost everywhere matches the Lean structure, with the density serving as a witness to class membership.

ass:iid-trial-sampling.detail: Lean defines the trial sample law as the product of n copies of the released observation law under each probability law P.

def:honest-procedures.detail: The uniform coverage condition matches Lean, with measurable bounded interval procedures represented by IntervalProcedure.

def:minimax-honest-length.detail: The Lean definition takes the infimum over honest release–interval pairs of the worst-case expected interval length.

ass:external-log-iid.detail: For each admissible external causal-law pair, Lean requires the score-log marginal to equal the product of m copies of H.

lem:fixed-released-law-baseline.detail: The hypotheses, quantile endpoints, attainable mean and ATE intervals, and endpoint witnesses match the listed Lean declarations.

lem:paired-high-resolution-quantization.detail: The mapped Lean declarations establish both limits, the equal-mass ordered boundaries, and the admissibility of the stated partition and midpoints under exactly the paper’s assumptions.

lem:external-two-source-lower-certificat.detail: The sampling assumptions, separation and certificate constants, risk bounds, and asymptotic limits match the listed Lean declarations.

def:external-normalized-risk.detail: The Lean normalizer is the reciprocal of the sum of the two inverse square-root sample sizes, and it multiplies the external excess risk as stated.

def:external-projection-handle.detail: The paper’s sieve, empirical measures, ball radii, projected intervals, and totalization match the mapped Lean definitions.

oeq:external-score-projection.detail: The paper poses the same open full-class and subclass sharp-limit questions as ExternalSharpLimitQuestion, without asserting a limit.

def:high-resolution-handle.detail: Both descriptions give uncrossing of measurable release cells followed by scalar quantization on ordered cells as the high-resolution proof strategy.

thm:universal-point-identification.detail: Both equivalences match the Lean theorem, including probability, measurability, overlap, and the positive-mass cell condition.

def:k-label-releases.detail: The paper defines the measurable maps from the score interval to a K-element label set, matching the three Lean definitions up to relabeling Fin K as {1,…,K}.

def:optimal-k-ambiguity.detail: The display defines exactly the infimum of worst-case ambiguity over measurable releases with K labels, matching the Lean definition.

thm:k-label-rate.detail: The paper carries the Lean hypotheses by statement or referenced definition, and its lower bound, upper bounds, measurability claim, and equal-width release agree with the mapped declarations up to one-based label notation.

thm:all-label-ambiguity.detail: The stated assumptions, ambiguity formula, half-Bernoulli released law, sharp interval length, and compatible endpoint attainments match the mapped Lean declarations.

thm:sharp-high-resolution-constant.detail: The paper matches the Lean hypotheses, limit constant, and existence of measurable releases with interval label cells.

prop:compatibility.detail: The paper states the same nonemptiness equivalence, with the Lean overlap and measurability hypotheses and matching label and treated-arm cell masses.

thm:minimax-honest-length.detail: The hypotheses, bounds, quantifiers, and explicit interval match the mapped Lean declarations; the reader-facing name \operatorname{clampATE} exposes a Lean identifier.

thm:external-score-root-order.detail: The paper carries the Lean hypotheses and matches its constants, finite-sample bounds, interval guarantee, and asymptotic bounds.

synth_1.detail: The paper defines the average treatment effect as the same integral of the two potential-outcome coordinates as Lean’s ate definition.

lem:released-arm-cell-masses.detail: The cited causal-law class supplies the Lean hypotheses, and the lemma establishes probability normalization and the stated arm-cell mass identity for every arm and label.
